title: asq Office terminal WebSocket frames
description: The JSON text frames of /ws/term/{id} (data-contract.md §8 for the v1.3 read path, backend-v1.4.md §6 for versioned input). Read-only v1.3 remains supported unchanged: a client that only reads frame/prompt/state/closing needs nothing new. Versioned INPUT is what 1.4 changes — every input frame carries a client-generated request_id, and the server answers that id with a receipt or an operation frame. A reconnect never blindly resends raw input. This file has no root body; each direction names a $defs pointer.

RequestId.description: Client-generated, unique within the socket. The back-end derives a stable transport-namespaced coordinator key from it, so a WS input reserves an operation exactly the way an HTTP Idempotency-Key does — no mutation reaches the coordinator without a resolved internal key. Reusing a request_id with a different frame body is 409-equivalent: an error frame with code idempotency_conflict.

oneOf.title: frame
oneOf.description: A full pane capture, ANSI kept; sent only when changed, at most 10/s.

oneOf.title: nopane
oneOf.description: origin "self": there is nothing to attach to. The connection stays open and sends no frames.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: 1.4 adds the optional code and request_id so a refused input frame can be blamed precisely — stale_prompt, contract_revision_required, idempotency_conflict — instead of only a sentence.

oneOf.title: closing
oneOf.description: v1.3 — the server is closing this socket on purpose.

oneOf.title: prompt
oneOf.description: v1.1 — the server's current reading of the prompt on screen, null when none. At 1.4 the Question carries prompt_id, which is the id an answer frame must quote.

oneOf.title: receipt
oneOf.description: The completed answer to one input frame. request_id is required at 1.4 so the client can match it; the work is done and the Receipt says what happened.

oneOf.title: operation
oneOf.description: 1.4 — the WS twin of a 202: the input was accepted but its outcome is not settled. The client polls GET /api/operations/{id}. It must not redraw the pane as if the input landed, and must not resend the frame.

ClientFrame.title: ClientFrame
ClientFrame.description: Client → server. scroll is read-only and needs no request_id. Every other frame here mutates the pane and requires one at revision 1.4; sent without it, the server answers an error frame with code contract_revision_required and types nothing.

oneOf.title: scroll
oneOf.description: v1.3, read-only: show the screen as it was `before` lines above the live view (0 = live).

oneOf.title: chip
oneOf.description: A named key chip. At 1.4 it also carries prompt_id when the chip answers a prompt, so a chip cannot land on a prompt that already left the pane.

oneOf.title: answer
oneOf.description: The structured resolve, over the socket. The body is the same ResolveRequest the HTTP route takes, so there is one normative answer shape and not a second WS-only vocabulary.
